issues.title: `torch.compile` causes segmentation fault with simple `ModuleList` model after multiple compile calls
issues.author: tinywisdom
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Issue Description
When compiling a simple convolutional model using `torch.compile` multiple times (including the `inductor` backend) and then running with CUDA, a segmentation fault occurs.

The script below is minimal and consistently reproduces the issue.
No error message is produced other than `Segmentation fault (core dumped)`.

## Minimal Reproduction Script
```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.nn import ModuleList
import torch.testing


class MyModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.layers = ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3, 3, kernel_size=3, padding=1) for _ in range(2)])

    def forward(self, x):
        for layer in self.layers:
            x = layer(x)
        return x


def my_model_function():
    return MyModel()


def GetInput():
    return torch.randn(1, 3, 224, 224, dtype=torch.float32)


def trigger_known_bugs(model=None):
    if model is None:
        model = my_model_function()
    input = GetInput()
    print("===1===")
    compiled_model = torch.compile(model)
    print("===2===")
    # Inductor backend test
    inductor_model = torch.compile(model, backend='inductor')
    print("===3===")
    inductor_output = inductor_model(input)
    print("===4===")
    model_cuda = model.to('cuda')
    input_cuda = input.to('cuda')
    print("===5===")
    compiled_model.train()
    print("===6===")
    _ = compiled_model(input)
    print("===7===")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import os

    os.environ["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = str("3")
    trigger_known_bugs()
```

## Observed Behavior
Output before crash:
```
===1===
===2===
===3===
===4===
===5===
===6===
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```



### Versions

```
PyTorch version: 2.7.1a0+gite2d141d & 2.8.0a0+gitba56102
Is debug build: True
CUDA used to build PyTorch: 12.6
ROCM used to build PyTorch: N/A

OS: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS (x86_64)
GCC version: (Ubuntu 12.3.0-1ubuntu1~22.04) 12.3.0
Clang version: Could not collect
CMake version: version 3.22.1
Libc version: glibc-2.35

Python version: 3.10.16 (main, Dec 11 2024, 16:24:50) [GCC 11.2.0] (64-bit runtime)
Python platform: Linux-6.8.0-59-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35
Is CUDA available: True
```

cc @chauhang @penguinwu

comments.author: yf225
comments.body:
Root cause:
- At the beginning, `model` is on CPU.
- After `compiled_model = torch.compile(model)`, `model` has its compiled CPU version (C++ code) stored in an internal attribute.
- Then, with `model_cuda = model.to('cuda')`, model weights are moved to CUDA (note that `model.to(...)` is an *in-place* operation).
- And then when running the compiled CPU version (C++ code) with CUDA weights, it throws error due to CPU and CUDA tensors not interchangeable.

For better error message, theoretically we could add device check to Inductor CPP generated code. But I am also not sure if it would increase overhead.

issues.title: Triton/Inductor Gather Prologue Fusion Issues
issues.author: eellison
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

I have a mostly ready PR implementing prologue fusion at https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/134532/ (although not yet ready for review). 

One of the use cases @Chillee pointed out was fusing a gather into a MM. For

```Python
torch.set_default_device("cuda)
x = torch.rand([2048, 2048], dtype=torch.float16)
y = torch.rand([2048, 2048], dtype=torch.float16)    
index = torch.randperm(2048, device="cuda")
def foo(x, y, index):
    return x[index] @ y
```

On an a100, When this is run on fp32, everything works succesfully. However, when run on fp16, I get the following error:

> python: /home/eellison/triton/third_party/nvidia/lib/TritonNVIDIAGPUToLLVM/LoadStoreOpToLLVM.cpp:852: virtual mlir::LogicalResult {anonymous}::AsyncCopyGlobalToLocalOpConversion::matchAndRewrite(mlir::triton::gpu::AsyncCopyGlobalToLocalOp, mlir::ConvertOpToLLVMPattern<mlir::triton::gpu::AsyncCopyGlobalToLocalOp>::OpAdaptor, mlir::ConversionPatternRewriter&) const: Assertion `byteWidth == 16 || byteWidth == 8 || byteWidth == 4' failed.

For this [generated kernel](https://gist.github.com/eellison/ca959f32ff25bb9afab276b2b49d36a4).

The main loop of the mm kernel is:

```Python
    for k_idx in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):

        a_k_idx_vals = offs_k[None, :] + (k_idx * BLOCK_K)
        idx_m = offs_a_m[:, None]
        idx_n = a_k_idx_vals
        xindex = idx_n + (2048*idx_m)
        tmp0 = tl.load(in_ptr1 + (tl.broadcast_to(idx_m, xindex.shape)), None, eviction_policy='evict_last')
        tmp1 = tl.full(xindex.shape, 2048, tl.int32)
        tmp2 = tmp0 + tmp1
        tmp3 = tmp0 < 0
        tmp4 = tl.where(tmp3, tmp2, tmp0)
        tl.device_assert((0 <= tl.broadcast_to(tmp4, xindex.shape)) & (tl.broadcast_to(tmp4, xindex.shape) < 2048), "index out of bounds: 0 <= tl.broadcast_to(tmp4, xindex.shape) < 2048")
        tmp6 = tl.load(in_ptr2 + (tl.broadcast_to(idx_n + (2048*tmp4), xindex.shape)), None, eviction_policy='evict_last')
        a = tmp6.to(tl.float16)

        B_ptr = B + ((offs_k[:, None] + (k_idx * BLOCK_K)) * stride_bk + offs_b_n[None, :] * stride_bn)

        b = tl.load(B_ptr)

        acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=ALLOW_TF32)
``` 


In this case, the `tmp0` load is loop invariant. When you [update the kernel](https://gist.github.com/eellison/885fede92f970060ef694d1eb0da5757) to hoist the load, it runs successfully. It also gives a 14% speedup over the max-autotune-no-cudagraphs without prologue fusion and 25% over eager.

So there are two issues here:

1) the codegen failure

2) Can triton improve its loop invariant code motion to hoist this load ? Note, we benchmark this prologue fusion, so in the worst case where we can't prove a hoist we would just not fuse instead of generating a terrible mm.

While it is doable for inductor to generate the code hoisted, this is code generated through triton templates. Ideally I would be to keep the single per buffer current prologue fusion api of `{{load_input("A", "a", ("idx_m", "idx_n")}}` instead of something more tedious that involved using apis for the initialization of indices. 

Not sure I file here or triton.. doing here for now.

issues.title: `torch._inductor.utils.fresh_cache` fails due to persistant process pool
issues.author: Flamefire
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Consider this code:

```python
import torch
from torch._inductor.utils import fresh_cache

def my_addmm(x, a, b, alpha, beta):
    return torch.addmm(x, a, b, alpha=beta, beta=alpha)

x = torch.randn((128, 128)).cuda().half()
a = torch.randn(128, 128).cuda().half()
b = torch.randn(128, 128).cuda().half().t()

with fresh_cache():
        torch.compile(my_addmm, dynamic=False)(x, a, b, 1.0, 2.0)
torch.compile(my_addmm, dynamic=False)(x, a, b, 1.0, 2.0)
```

The first `torch.compile` will cause creation of a `TuningProcessPool` through `torch/_inductor/autotune_process.benchmark_in_sub_process`

On exit the cache directory is deleted but the subprocesses don't get the updated/reset `$TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` value still using the old, non-existing cache folder and may subsequently fail with a `FileNotFound` error

This was observed in `inductor/test_cutlass_backend` with a workaround placed by @kadeng: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/8f96e7bc1dff48a8a9b3800b018ef856acf94d69/test/inductor/test_cutlass_backend.py#L169-L178


The test still fails when the whole test file is run because some tests use `fresh_cache()`, e.g. https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/4de24bcc569ec19b20756e3aa01f874bc435555d/test/inductor/test_cutlass_backend.py#L1155

Depending on the test order this causes FileNotFound errors in e.g. `TestCutlassBackend.test_fp8_rowwise_scaling_float8_e4m3fn_shape0_has_bias_False_use_fast_accum_True_float16` even though that doesn't use `fresh_cache` itself.

I think this is a different failure. What I was talking about was that PyTorch spawns subprocesses and then changes the environment of the main process via `fresh_cache` which is not reflected in the subprocesses.
So on the next calls any access to files in `cache_dir()`, which is used in pretty much all `CodeCaches`, will be subject to race conditions or hard failures.

However it seems this has indeed been addressed: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/167918
There it passes the env variable to the process explicitely, so I guess this resolves the issue.

As it is hard to make it cause a hard error in a reproducible way I'm not sure if this is indeed resolved, but it looks like it is

issues.title: `torch.compile` (Inductor) fails on MKL-DNN tensor densify (`to_dense`) with "Cannot access data pointer of Tensor that doesn't have storage"
issues.author: tinywisdom
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

When running a simple model that converts an MKL-DNN tensor to dense (`x.to_dense()`) and then applies an elementwise operation, eager mode works fine.
However, with `torch.compile` (default Inductor backend), execution fails with:
```
RuntimeError: Cannot access data pointer of Tensor that doesn't have storage
```

+ Eager and `backend="aot_eager"` both succeed.
+ The error is reproducible on PyTorch 2.8 .

This suggests Inductor’s handling of `mkldnn` layout tensors is incomplete/inconsistent when lowering `to_dense()`.

## Minimal Reproduction Script
```python
# repro_mkldnn_to_dense_compile.py
import torch
from torch import nn

class MyModel(nn.Module):
    def forward(self, x):
        x = x.to_dense()   # densify MKL-DNN tensor
        return x + 1       # simple elementwise op

def get_input():
    x = torch.randn(4, 4)
    x_mkldnn = x.to_mkldnn()     # construct mkldnn layout input
    assert x_mkldnn.is_mkldnn
    return x_mkldnn

def main():
    model = MyModel().eval()
    inp = get_input()

    # 1) Eager mode
    eager_out = model(inp)
    expected = inp.to_dense() + 1
    torch.testing.assert_close(eager_out, expected)
    print("[eager] OK, out shape:", tuple(eager_out.shape), "is_mkldnn:", eager_out.is_mkldnn)

    # 2) AOT-Eager backend
    compiled_ok = torch.compile(model, backend="aot_eager")
    out_ok = compiled_ok(inp.to_dense())  # feeding dense also works
    torch.testing.assert_close(out_ok, expected)
    print("[compile:aot_eager] OK, out shape:", tuple(out_ok.shape), "is_mkldnn:", out_ok.is_mkldnn)

    # 3) Inductor (default)
    compiled = torch.compile(model)  # backend='inductor'
    out = compiled(inp)              # <-- RuntimeError here
    torch.testing.assert_close(out, expected)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`torch.compile` with the Inductor backend crashes on a model that converts an MKLDNN tensor to dense and then applies simple arithmetic.

Eager execution succeeds and returns a strided tensor. The compiled version fails with: `RuntimeError: Cannot access data pointer of Tensor that doesn't have storage`

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class M(nn.Module):
    def forward(self, x):
        return x.to_dense() * 2 - 1

    raise SystemExit(2)

x = (torch.arange(9, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(3, 3) / 3).to_mkldnn()

    eager = f"OK {eager_out.layout} {eager_out}"
except Exception as exc:
    eager = f"{type(exc).__name__} {str(exc).splitlines()[0]}"

    compiled_out = torch.compile(
        model,
        backend="inductor",
        fullgraph=True,
        dynamic=True,

    compiled = f"OK {compiled_out.layout} {compiled_out}"
except Exception as exc:
    compiled = f"{type(exc).__name__} {str(exc).splitlines()[0]}"

print("input_layout:", x.layout)
print("eager:", eager)
print("compiled:", compiled)
```

issues.author: tinywisdom
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`torch.compile` fails when compiling a minimal model that takes an MKL-DNN tensor, explicitly converts it to a dense strided tensor with `to_dense()`, and then applies a simple elementwise operation.

The same model runs successfully in eager mode. In eager mode, the input layout is `torch._mkldnn`, and after `x.to_dense()`, the output layout becomes `torch.strided`. However, the compiled path fails during the generated Inductor kernel execution with:

```text
RuntimeError: Cannot access data pointer of Tensor that doesn't have storage
This suggests that the compiled path may not be correctly handling the layout/storage transition caused by to_dense() on an MKL-DNN tensor.
```

### Minimal repro
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-

import os
import json
import platform
import traceback

import torch
import torch.nn as nn


SEED = 0


class MyModel(nn.Module):
    def forward(self, x):
        x = x.to_dense()
        return x + 1


def my_model_function():
    return MyModel()


def GetInput():
    x = torch.randn(4, 4)
    return x.to_mkldnn()


def print_runtime_info():
    info = {
        "python": platform.python_version(),
        "platform": platform.platform(),
        "torch_version": torch.__version__,
        "cuda_available": torch.cuda.is_available(),
        "cuda_device_count": torch.cuda.device_count(),
        "cuda_visible_devices": os.environ.get("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES", ""),
        "mkldnn_available": torch.backends.mkldnn.is_available(),
        "mkldnn_enabled": torch.backends.mkldnn.enabled,
        "seed": SEED,
        "compile_config": {
            "fullgraph": True,
            "dynamic": True,
        },
    }

    print("[runtime]")
    print(json.dumps(info, indent=2, sort_keys=True))


def describe_tensor(name, x):
    print(f"\n[{name}]")
    print("shape:", tuple(x.shape))
    print("dtype:", x.dtype)
    print("device:", x.device)
    print("layout:", x.layout)
    if hasattr(x, "is_mkldnn"):
        print("is_mkldnn:", x.is_mkldnn)


def main():
    print_runtime_info()

    if not torch.backends.mkldnn.is_available():
        print("\n[SKIP] MKL-DNN is not available in this PyTorch build.")
        return

    torch.manual_seed(SEED)

    model = my_model_function().eval()
    x = GetInput()

    describe_tensor("input", x)

    try:
        with torch.no_grad():
            eager_out = model(x)

        describe_tensor("eager output", eager_out)
        print(eager_out)

    except Exception:
        print("\n[ERROR] eager execution failed")
        traceback.print_exc()
        return

    try:
        compiled_model = torch.compile(
            model,
            fullgraph=True,
            dynamic=True,
        )

        with torch.no_grad():
            compiled_out = compiled_model(x)

        describe_tensor("compiled output", compiled_out)
        print(compiled_out)

        print("\n[comparison]")
        print("same_shape:", eager_out.shape == compiled_out.shape)
        print("same_dtype:", eager_out.dtype == compiled_out.dtype)
```

comments.body:
Update: When compiling with CUDA 13.2, we need
```python3
if os.name == "nt":
    NVCC_FLAGS += [
        "-Xcompiler=/Zc:preprocessor",
        "-D_WIN32=1",
        "-DUSE_CUDA=1",
    ]
```
Otherwise the non-standard preprocessor in MSVC called by nvcc will have trouble with `std`.

By the way, if we see
```python3
ABI = 1 if torch._C._GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI else 0
CXX_FLAGS += [f"-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI={ABI}"]
NVCC_FLAGS_COMMON += [f"-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI={ABI}"]
```
we need to replace with
```python3
if os.name != "nt":
    ABI = 1 if torch._C._GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI else 0
    CXX_FLAGS += [f"-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI={ABI}"]
    NVCC_FLAGS_COMMON += [f"-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI={ABI}"]
```
Because CXX11 ABI does not make sense on Windows, and it seems to cause nvcc going into some wrong codepath.

This issue still exists as of torch 2.12.0 . It's not strictly a bug of torch, but MSVC default behavior that's not compliant with C++ standard, and we need the workaround anyway.

comments.author: Sahil170595
comments.body:
No attachment to 14.42, it is just what `vcvars64` picked. The version dependence is testable though, so I tested it. The same one-line repro (details in the PR) fires identically on every MSVC line I can find a data point for:

| MSVC toolset | cl | ships with | source | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 14.42.34433 | 19.42 | VS 2022 17.12 | my box | C2872 |
| 14.43.34808 | 19.43 | VS 2022 17.13 | this issue's original traceback above | C2872 |
| 14.44.35217 | 19.44 | VS 2022 17.14, current | my box, just verified | C2872 |
| 14.50.35717 | 19.50 | VS 18 Community | #173232's traceback | C2872 |

So it does not look like an old-compiler artifact: the current VS 2022 toolset and the newest VS 18 toolset both hit it.

One more constraint on the "use a newer compiler" path: CUDA 13.0's `crt/host_config.h` hard-errors on `_MSC_VER >= 1950`, so VS 2022 toolsets (14.2x to 14.4x) are the newest host compilers nvcc officially supports there (newer toolkits may raise the ceiling), and per #173232 the 14.50 toolset reproduces anyway.

Agreed that PyTorch should not chase every buggy MSVC. The reason I would still fix this one: it fires on all currently supported host compilers for the default `torch.utils.cpp_extension` path, and the fix is a semantics-preserving rearrangement rather than a compiler workaround: the construct just moves out of the always-instantiated template path.
